headline_marked: Citizen committee [[raises 19 questions over police probe]] into Rangpur family killings
headline: Citizen committee raises 19 questions over police probe into Rangpur family killings
summary: The committee challenges the police's narrative on the murder of a retired teacher, his wife, daughter, and son, citing contradictions in evidence and forensics.
details: A citizen committee in Rangpur has raised 19 critical questions regarding the police investigation into the brutal murder of retired teacher Ganapati Chakraborty, his wife Pritilata, daughter Agami, and son Ayush.

The committee, led by Advocate Palash Kanti Nag and Professor Mozahar Ali, held a press conference on Saturday to challenge the police's claims about how two teenagers were able to kill four people using only towels and ropes.

Key contradictions highlighted include the police's claim that the house's electricity was cut off, while Facebook messages from the daughter's friend show she was active online until 5:50 AM, suggesting the family was alive longer than reported.

The committee questioned why the police attributed the motive to drug use, questioning why the killers would risk entering a residential home rather than a nearby empty building if drug use was the primary goal.

Serious concerns were raised about the missing CCTV footage from the temple in front of the house and the missing 1.5 million BDT provident fund money that the teacher had recently withdrawn from the bank.

The committee also pointed out conflicting forensic reports: one expert claimed sperm was found on the bodies of the mother and daughter, while another forensic officer from Rangpur Medical College Hospital denied any evidence of rape.

Further doubts were raised about the police's timeline of the suspects' escape, noting that the police claimed they left during Friday prayers, yet the area is predominantly Hindu and has no nearby mosque.

The committee expressed concern over the police's rapid identification of the suspects, questioning how they were identified so quickly before DNA or fingerprint reports from the CID laboratory could have typically been returned.

They also highlighted a discrepancy in the clothing worn by the suspect Siddhartha Das during his arrest, claiming he was seen wearing a police officer's shirt after his arrest, which they claim adds to the uncertainty of the police narrative.

headline_marked: 996 hospitalised as [[two more die of dengue]] in 24 hours
headline: 996 hospitalised as two more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: Total deaths this year have risen to 90, with over 33,000 cases recorded according to the DGHS.
details: At least two dengue patients died and 996 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am today.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the deaths were reported in the Barishal division.
With these new additions, the total number of dengue deaths this year has risen to 90, while the total number of cases has reached 33,586.
Currently, 2,101 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in various hospitals across the country.
